nodes.name: FeNi2-MIL-88B/NF Solvothermal
nodes.procedure: Terephthalic acid (0.83 g, 5.0 mmol), FeCl3·6H2O (0.45 g, 6.6 mmol), and Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.97 g, 3.3 mmol) were dissolved in DMF (25 mL) solution, then NaOH (2 mL, 2.0 M) was added with stirring for 30 min. The above solution with NF was then transferred into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless autoclave and heated at 100°C for 15 h. Finally, the FeNi2-MIL-88B/NF was obtained by drying in a vacuum oven at 60°C for 12 h.

Finally, the FeNi2-MIL-88B/NF was obtained by drying in a vacuum oven at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Phosphorization to Phosphides
nodes.procedure: All the metal phosphides were prepared by solid phosphorization process. Briefly, the as synthesized samples (FeNi2/NF, Ru-Ni(OH)2/NF, and Ru-FeNi2/NF) were heated to 350°C for 4 h in the argon filed tube furnace with NaH2PO2·H2O as phosphorus source. After natural cooling, the Ni2P/Fe2P/NF, Ru-Ni2P/NF and Ru-Ni2P/Fe2P/NF were obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms the porous structure of Ru-Ni2P/Fe2P nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) results confirm the porous structure of Ru - Ni2P / Fe2P nanosheets (Figure 1e,f; Figure S6, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms (111) planes of Ni2P and Fe2P with distinct heterogeneous interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Zooming into the network structure of Ru - Ni2P / Fe2P by high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), the (111) planes of Ni2P and Fe2P can be confirmed (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping confirms uniform distributions of Ni, Fe, P, and Ru elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping results (Figure 1h), the uniform distributions of Ni, Fe, P, and Ru elements in the Ru - Ni2P / Fe2P were confirmed.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern indexed to Ni2P and Fe2P phases with peaks at 44.5° and 51.8° from NF (111) and (200) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern in Figure 2a is indexed to Ni₂P and Fe₂P, in which peaks at 44.5° and 51.8° belong to the (111) and (200) crystal planes of the NF (JCPDS 04-0850).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Ni, Fe, P elements; Ni 2p peaks at 853.3 eV (Ni-P), 856.8 eV (oxidized Ni), 861.6 eV (satellite) with 0.2 eV negative shift due to Ru doping; Fe 2p and P 2p (129.6 eV metal-P, 134.1 eV P-O) confirm phosphide formation; no Ru signal detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of Ni, Fe, and P elements in the catalyst can be confirmed by the survey XPS spectrum... For Ni 2p high-resolution XPS spectra of Ru - Ni₂P / Fe₂P, three peaks located at 853.3, 856.8, and 861.6 eV are assigned to Ni-P, oxidized Ni species and satellite Ni peak, respectively... In comparison with Ni₂P / Fe₂P, a negative shift of 0.2 eV is observed in Ru - Ni₂P / Fe₂P... The P 2p XPS spectrum can be deconvoluted into two peaks, in which the peak at 129.6 eV corresponds to metal-P and the peak at 134.1 eV belongs to the P - O bond... No signal of Ru is detected by XPS.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru mass ratio determined to be 0.0591 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the result of inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), the mass ratio of Ru in the electrocatalyst is determined to be 0.0591 wt.%

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge absorption edge between RuO2 and Ru foil indicates Ru valence between 0 and +4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As seen from Figure 2e, the absorption edge of Ru - Ni2P / Fe2P is located between RuO2 and Ru foil, indicating that the valence state of Ru is between 0 and +4

nodes.characterization_summary: FT k³-weighted EXAFS shows Ru-P bond at ≈1.75 Å and Ru-metal bond at ≈2.26 Å; absence of Ru-Ru coordination at ≈2.35 Å confirms atomically dispersed Ru; WT confirms Ru-P coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier-transformed k³-weighted EXAFS spectra were collected to deeply understand the local coordination environment of Ru, in which two peaks at ≈ 1.75 and ≈ 2.26Å could be attributed to the Ru - P bond and Ru-metal bond, respectively... The Ru - Ru coordination in the metallic state (≈ 2.35Å) is absent for Ru - Ni₂P / Fe₂P, suggesting the atomically dispersed Ru in samples... For Ru - Ni₂P / Fe₂P, the signal intensity maximum located at ≈ 6Å is obviously different from RuO₂, proving the presence of Ru - P coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows peaks at 479.4 and 555.3 cm⁻¹ at 1.45 V corresponding to NiOOH vibrations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ, Raman spectra were applied... two additional peaks at 479.4 and 555.3 cm⁻¹ appear with increasing potential to 1.45 V, corresponding to the bending vibration of Eg (δ(Ni-O)) and the tensile vibration of A1g (ν(Ni-O)) for NiOOH, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl values of 21.21 mF cm⁻² for HER and 46.9 mF cm⁻² for OER, indicating larger ECSA than Ru-Ni2P and Ni2P/Fe2P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru - Ni₂P / Fe₂P exhibits a Cdl value of 21.21 and 46.9 mF cm⁻² for HER and OER, which is obviously larger than that of Ru-Ni₂P and Ni₂P/Fe₂P (Figures S13 and S14, Supporting Information).
